surfaces.part: dirt ground with asphalt road patches seen from above

answer.evidence: The image is a full-bleed 176x192 flat terrain tile showing a top-down road network of cracked asphalt patches (crossroads, T-junctions, dead ends) on a dirt base. The silhouette is a uniform 176 wide for all rows, so there is no standing object, no front face and no eave or edge line. It is a ground texture. It has no vertical south face, so it reads as a flat top-down surface, which fits the terrain kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 6 visible tones per tile, between the grass reference (3) and the paving reference (7). Near-flat coverage is 1% and the dark edge pixels are fully tinted (0% neutral), so the edges lean toward the material tone rather than a neutral black line. The structure is thinner than the references, though. The whole patch uses only 12 distinct colours. The dirt is roughly 4-5 browns scattered as random speckle, with no clumps, pebbles or grain shaped by hand. The asphalt patches are blobs of about 3-4 blue-grey steps, with a darker rim and sparse light flecks, and no per-stone or per-chunk shading like the paving reference's 6-7 steps. The cracks and the crumbling into dirt are not drawn as readable forms. The patches read as flat cut-outs laid on a noise background, which is closer to the shallow sticker look than to Beodeul craft.
